parametric-circles-lines-s1.title: A circle with a starting point
parametric-circles-lines-s1.text: A point travels once around the circle shown for $0 \le t \le 2\pi$, starting at the marked point and moving counterclockwise.

parametric-circles-lines-s2.title: A drone flight
parametric-circles-lines-s2.text: A drone flies in a straight line at a steady pace from $(-2, 5)$ at $t = 0$ to $(6, 1)$ at $t = 4$ seconds. Coordinates are in meters.

items.q: Which parametric function traces the circle as shown?

why.correct: The center is $(2, 1)$ and the radius is $3$. $(2 + 3\cos t, 1 + 3\sin t)$ starts at $(5, 1)$ when $t = 0$ and moves counterclockwise.
options: With $1 - 3\sin t$ the point moves down first from $(5, 1)$: clockwise.
This starts at $(2, 4)$, the top, and moves clockwise.
The radius multiplies $\cos t$ and $\sin t$; $9$ is the radius squared.

why.correct: $x = 2 + 3\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 2 + 0 = 2$ and $y = 1 + 3\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1 + 3 = 4$: the top of the circle, a quarter turn counterclockwise from the start.
options: A quarter turn counterclockwise from $(5, 1)$ is the top, $(2, 4)$.

items.q: For which values of $t$ is the point on the upper half of the circle, $y \ge 1$?

why.correct: $y = 1 + 3\sin t \ge 1$ exactly when $\sin t \ge 0$, which on $[0, 2\pi]$ is $0 \le t \le \pi$.
options: On this interval $\cos t \le 0$: the left half.
This is only the upper right quarter.

items.q: Which change makes the point travel clockwise around the same circle, starting at the same point?
options: Replace the $3$ with $-3$ in both coordinates

why.correct: With $y = 1 - 3\sin t$ the start is still $(5, 1)$, but just after $t = 0$ the point moves down: clockwise.
options: $x$ is unchanged, so the start stays $(5, 1)$, and the point moves down first.
This starts at $(-1, 1)$, a different point.
This goes around twice, still counterclockwise.
This starts at $(-1, 1)$ and still goes counterclockwise.

items.q: What is the $x$-coordinate of the point when $t = \frac{\pi}{3}$?

mistakes.why: $8$ is the whole change in $x$ over $4$ seconds; per second it is $\frac{8}{4} = 2$.
This starts at $x = 6$; the drone starts at $(-2, 5)$.
At $t = 0$ the drone is at $x = -2$: add the starting value.

why.correct: $x$ goes from $-2$ to $6$, a change of $8$, in $4$ seconds: $2$ per second. $x(t) = -2 + 2t$.

mistakes.why: $-4$ is the whole change in $y$; per second it is $\frac{-4}{4} = -1$.
This goes from $y = 1$ to $y = 5$, backward. Start at $5$.
$y$ falls from $5$ to $1$, so the rate is negative.

why.correct: $y$ goes from $5$ to $1$, a change of $-4$, in $4$ seconds: $-1$ per second. $y(t) = 5 - t$.
$x(1) = -2 + 2(1) = 0$ and $y(1) = 5 - 1 = 4$. After one quarter of the trip it is one quarter of the way: $(0, 4)$.

items.q: What is the slope of the drone's path?

mistakes.why: Slope is the rate of $y$ over the rate of $x$: $\frac{-1}{2}$, not $\frac{2}{-1}$.
$-1$ is the rate of $y$ per second. Divide it by the rate of $x$, $2$.

why.correct: $\frac{\text{rate of } y}{\text{rate of } x} = \frac{-1}{2}$, the same as $\frac{1 - 5}{6 - (-2)} = -\frac{4}{8}$.

items.q: How does $(\cos t, \sin t)$ for $0 \le t \le 2\pi$ trace the unit circle?
options: It starts at $(1, 0)$ and goes once around counterclockwise
It starts at $(0, 1)$ and goes once around clockwise
It starts at $(1, 0)$ and goes once around clockwise
It starts at $(0, 1)$ and goes once around counterclockwise

why.correct: At $t = 0$ the point is $(\cos 0, \sin 0) = (1, 0)$; at $t = \frac{\pi}{2}$ it is $(0, 1)$. Right to top is counterclockwise.
options: $(0, 1)$ is the start of $(\sin t, \cos t)$.
From $(1, 0)$ the point rises toward $(0, 1)$, which is counterclockwise.

items.q: How many times does $(3\cos 2t, 3\sin 2t)$ go around its circle for $0 \le t \le 2\pi$?

why.correct: The angle is $2t$, which runs from $0$ to $4\pi$: two full turns.
options: One turn needs $2t$ to cover $2\pi$, which takes only $0 \le t \le \pi$.
$4\pi$ of angle is two turns, not four.
Doubling the angle speeds the point up; it goes around more, not less.

items.q: Describe the trip traced by $(4\sin t, 4\cos t)$ for $0 \le t \le 2\pi$.
options: It starts at $(0, 4)$ and goes once around clockwise
It starts at $(4, 0)$ and goes once around counterclockwise
It starts at $(0, 4)$ and goes once around counterclockwise
It starts at $(4, 0)$ and goes once around clockwise

why.correct: At $t = 0$: $(0, 4)$, the top. At $t = \frac{\pi}{2}$: $(4, 0)$, the right side. Top to right is clockwise.
options: That describes $(4\cos t, 4\sin t)$; here sine comes first.
From the top the point moves to the right side, which is clockwise.

items.q: For $(4\cos t, 4\sin t)$, what is the $y$-coordinate of the point when $t = \frac{\pi}{3}$?
Which parametric functions trace the segment from $(0, 0)$ to $(2, 4)$, starting at $(0, 0)$? Select all that apply.

why.correct: Each must start at $(0, 0)$ and end at $(2, 4)$. $(2t, 4t)$ on $[0, 1]$ ends at $(2, 4)$; $(t, 2t)$ on $[0, 2]$ ends at $(2, 4)$.
options: Ends at $(4, 2)$: the coordinates are swapped.

items.q: A line passes through $(1, 3)$ with slope $2$. If $x(t) = 1 + t$, write $y(t)$ so that $(x(t), y(t))$ traces the line and is at $(1, 3)$ when $t = 0$.

mistakes.why: Slope is rate of $y$ over rate of $x$. With $x$ changing by $1$ per unit of $t$, $y$ must change by $2$.
The starting value and the rate are swapped: start at $3$, change by $2$.

why.correct: $x$ changes by $1$ per unit of $t$, and slope $2$ means $y$ changes by $2$ for each $1$ of $x$. Start at $y = 3$: $y(t) = 3 + 2t$.

items.q: Which equation is satisfied by every point of $x(t) = -1 + 5\cos t$, $y(t) = 4 + 5\sin t$?

why.correct: $x + 1 = 5\cos t$ and $y - 4 = 5\sin t$. Squaring and adding: $25\cos^2 t + 25\sin^2 t = 25$, so $(x + 1)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 25$.
options: The center is $(-1, 4)$; $(x - 1)^2$ would put it at $x = 1$.
The right side is the radius squared, $5^2 = 25$.

items.q: In $(2 + r\cos t, 1 + r\sin t)$ for $0 \le t \le 2\pi$, $r$ is increased from $3$ to $5$. Predict each change.

variables.name: The distance from each point to the center
variables.why: Each point is $r$ units from $(2, 1)$, so the distance grows from $3$ to $5$.

variables.name: The center of the circle
variables.why: The center is the added part, $(2, 1)$, which does not depend on $r$.

variables.name: The interval of $t$ needed for one trip around
variables.why: One trip still takes $t$ from $0$ to $2\pi$; only the size changes.

why.correct: $r$ sets the size. The center and the parameter interval for one trip stay the same.
